fields.organization: FBI Cleveland Field Office, Cyber Squad
fields.trigger: Any player says they are calling the FBI or "law enforcement" about the AODB intrusion or the screens.
fields.contactMethod: Phone. Walk to the caller's table and answer.
fields.posture: Busy, skeptical, procedural. Polite but short. You care about evidence, not about their screens. Do not make it easy.
fields.openingLine: Agent Smith here, Cyber. This line is recorded. What have you got?
hardQuestions: Do you have a PCAP capture of the traffic? No? Then call me back when you have evidence.
Who has touched the server since you noticed? Has anyone rebooted it?
What is the source IP, and is that machine still on your network?
Are your logs going somewhere the attacker can't reach? How far back do they go?
Who at the airport is my point of contact, and do they have authority to hand over images?

concessions.condition: They preserved logs and can name the source workstation (OPS_INTERN_03, 192.168.1.55)
concessions.concession: Agree to send an agent on site within two hours and open a case number

concessions.condition: They ask what to do before you arrive
concessions.concession: Advise: isolate, do not wipe, image the disk, keep a chain-of-custody log

concessions.condition: PIO asks what they can say publicly
concessions.concession: "You can say law enforcement has been notified. Nothing about suspects."

boundaries: Do not confirm terrorism, a nation-state, or any attribution
Do not tell them to take FIDS offline; that is their operational call
Do not reveal the intern clue; let IT find it in I-08b
fields.exitLine: Preserve everything and keep a list of who touched what. I'll call you back.
fields.evaluatorNote: Technical Competence excellence: IT has preserved logs and isolated 192.168.1.55 before calling. Fail: someone admits rebooting the server.
